verdict.summary: Mercury has no self-serve OAuth console. You can't connect even your own account until you fill in a request form, Mercury approves it, and Mercury creates the client and sends you the credentials, encrypted to your GPG key. Mercury doesn't publish a timeline. Its docs mention no security assessment and no marketplace review. The partner OAuth flow only gives read and offline_access scopes.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 2-4 hours (form, legal/brand links, GPG key, Composio config, sandbox test)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Only after Mercury approves the request (no published timeline). After you receive credentials, about 30 min in the sandbox.
verdict.approval_wait: Unknown. Mercury says timelines depend on how complex the integration is, and it may ask for more information.

gates.name: Approved partner OAuth client (sandbox test client)
gates.unlocks: Mercury creates your OAuth client and sends you the client ID, client secret and sandbox test-client credentials, so you can authorize your own account through your app.
limits: Prior approval is required before any connection works
Access tokens expire after 1 hour. Refresh tokens expire after 720 hours and can be used only once.
Scopes are limited to read and offline_access
gates.time_to_reach: Depends on Mercury's approval (no published timeline), then about 30 min of setup

gates.name: Dev/test redirect URIs + sandbox
gates.unlocks: Test users can authorize through the dev/test redirect URIs you registered, using the sandbox.
limits: Mercury's docs list no user or install caps for unreviewed partner apps
The product page lists 100 free ACH transfers a month. That is a product quota, not an OAuth app limit.
Per-endpoint rate limits are not published
gates.time_to_reach: Same approval as Gate 1. You supply the dev/test redirect URIs after approval.

gates.name: Production OAuth client
gates.unlocks: Any Mercury customer can connect through your production redirect URI.
limits: Mercury's OAuth pages mention no marketplace listing, security assessment or app-store review
The read scope cannot do write operations such as payments or managing recipients
gates.time_to_reach: Comes with the same approval. To move from sandbox to production you change one URL.

steps.title: Confirm partner OAuth is the right track
steps.detail: Partner OAuth gives read-only access (accounts and transactions) and needs Mercury's approval. If you only need your own account, a scoped API token from Settings may be enough. If you want an agent to use Mercury through MCP, Mercury's hosted MCP server lets clients register themselves (Dynamic Client Registration) with nothing to set up on Mercury's side.
gotchas: Write actions such as payments and recipients are documented only for API token scopes, not OAuth scopes
API tokens with write scopes need an IP allowlist, and Mercury offers no way around it

steps.title: Draft the OAuth request form answers
steps.detail: Draft answers for: company name and website, company address, a short company description, the product you are integrating, and how you will use the API. Mercury weighs security, use-case fit and regulatory considerations, so state clearly that you need read-only access and explain why.

steps.title: Submit the Mercury OAuth Request Form
steps.detail: Open the 'Mercury OAuth Request Form' on Notion and submit your answers. The form loaded without a login.

steps.title: Wait for Mercury's approval
steps.detail: Mercury reviews the request. Timelines vary with integration complexity, and Mercury may ask for more information during review. Respond promptly.

steps.title: Prepare terms, privacy policy and logo links
steps.detail: After approval, Mercury asks for links to your app's terms of service, privacy policy and logo. Draft and publish these pages, and check that the URLs load publicly.

steps.title: Generate a GPG key pair
steps.detail: Mercury sends credentials securely and asks for a GPG public key. Generate a key pair, keep the private key safe, and send Mercury only the public key.

steps.title: Send Mercury your redirect URIs
steps.detail: Give Mercury the production redirect URI and, if you want them, dev/test redirect URIs. The redirect_url in the authorize request must match a registered callback exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Receive and decrypt credentials
steps.detail: Mercury creates the OAuth client and sends the client ID and client secret, plus sandbox test-client credentials, encrypted to your GPG key. Decrypt them and store them in a secrets manager.

steps.title: Configure your own OAuth credentials in Composio
steps.detail: Composio has no Mercury managed app, so you must use your own credentials. Enter the client ID and client secret in a custom auth config. Request both scopes, space-separated: read and offline_access. The flow supports the authorization code grant, with or without PKCE.
gotchas: offline_access must be in the client configuration and also in the request that starts the flow, or no refresh token is issued
The state parameter must be at least 8 characters

steps.title: Run a test authorization in the sandbox
steps.detail: Using the sandbox test client, complete an authorization, exchange the code for tokens, call a read endpoint, and run one refresh. Check that each refresh returns a new refresh token and that your code stores it.

steps.title: Switch to production
steps.detail: Change the sandbox URL to the production URL and use the production client credentials. Mercury's OAuth pages document no extra listing or review step.

requirements.item: Approved OAuth request form (company details, product, API use case)
requirements.detail: Prior approval is required before Mercury creates any OAuth client.

requirements.item: Production redirect URI (plus optional dev/test URIs)
requirements.detail: Must exactly match the redirect_url sent in authorize requests.

requirements.item: Public terms of service, privacy policy and logo links
requirements.detail: Requested after approval, before the client is created.
Used to deliver the client ID and secret securely.

scopes.effect: Read access to accounts and transactions. The only data scope available through partner OAuth, and covered by the prior-approval gate.
Issues refresh tokens. Must be in the client configuration and in the authorize request. Refresh tokens last 720 hours and can be used once each.

scopes.scope: transactions:request / transfers:request / categories:create / categories:edit / transactions:update (MCP only)
scopes.effect: Available only through the MCP server, not partner OAuth. Payment and transfer requests still need approval inside Mercury.

blockers.symptom: No credentials, and no console where you can create them
blockers.cause: Mercury has no self-serve OAuth console. Clients are created only after manual approval.
blockers.fix: Submit the request form, then answer any follow-up questions from Mercury promptly.

blockers.symptom: Your agent needs to send payments or manage recipients, but OAuth only offers read
blockers.cause: Write operations are documented under API token scopes, not partner OAuth scopes.
blockers.fix: Use the MCP track (write scopes, with payments approved in Mercury) or an API token. Write tokens require an IP allowlist.

blockers.symptom: Users must reconnect, or refreshes fail
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are single-use and expire after 720 hours. Without offline_access, no refresh token is issued.
blockers.fix: Request offline_access, save the new refresh token after every refresh, and prompt users to reconnect after 30 days without use.

blockers.cause: redirect_url doesn't match the registered URI, or state is shorter than 8 characters.
blockers.fix: Use the exact registered Composio callback URL and a state value of at least 8 characters.

blockers.cause: client_name starts with the word 'Mercury', or PKCE uses the 'plain' method.
blockers.fix: Choose a client name that doesn't start with 'Mercury', and use PKCE with S256.

composio.note: Composio has no Mercury toolkit or managed OAuth app, so there is no managed option to start on. You need your own partner OAuth client from Mercury, which requires prior approval, and then you enter its client ID and secret in Composio. Mercury's hosted MCP server, which uses Dynamic Client Registration with no pre-approval, is a separate track and does not provide partner API credentials.

open_questions: Mercury publishes no review timeline in days or weeks, only that it varies.
The partner OAuth authorize and token URLs (as opposed to the MCP endpoints) were not found in the official docs. Confirm them with Mercury when you receive credentials.
Composio has no Mercury toolkit. It is unclear whether Composio can run a custom OAuth integration for Mercury, or whether a managed app will ever exist.
It is not documented whether the request form requires a paid plan, an admin role or business verification.
Mercury's docs list no install or user caps for partner OAuth apps.
REST API and partner OAuth rate limits are not published.
No OpenID Connect support was found for the partner flow.
